label: letter l input during the original phase
explanation: Fires on every original-phase step whose input is the letter l (dev precision 1.00, recall 0.997), and on nothing else. It is silent on all other input tokens and at the <DEL> step. In the copy phase it is almost always silent, even when l is fed back or output; the only exceptions are about 330 weak activations near recall_idx 1. Activation is strongest (about max, 2.85) when l is the first token of the sequence (t=0). It weakens at later positions: activation mass falls off faster with t than the firing rate does, and late l tokens just before <DEL> are around 0.3-0.6 of max. It is also weaker on repeat occurrences of l (in_first=0, often 0.6-0.8 of max) than on the first one.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split there are 0 false positives and 393 missed steps, which hold 0.0% of the activation mass. All the misses shown are tiny activations (0.01-0.06 of max) at recall_idx 1, where the input is l fed back right after <DEL> in sequences that start with l. The explanation already describes these as about 330 weak copy-phase activations near recall_idx 1.

Magnitude claims check out. The top examples all have t=0 l at 1.00. Activation mass per firing drops with t: 0.204 of the mass over 16881 firings at t=0, versus 0.007 over 2695 at t=8. Late l tokens are around 0.27-0.6 of max. Repeat l tokens are weaker (in_first=0 holds 7.2% of mass across 10378 firings, versus 92.8% across 97997 for in_first=1).
Silent at <DEL> (0 of 500k steps) and on every other input token: confirmed.

Label matches the predicate. One small nuance: the firing rate on original-phase l is close to 100%, but magnitude depends on position and on whether this is the first l. The explanation already says this.
